questions.q: What does lazy evaluation mean in Spark?
options: Operations build up a plan, and nothing actually runs until an action explicitly requests a result
Spark runs every line of code immediately, just like Pandas
Lazy evaluation means Spark ignores half of the operations you write
It refers to Spark running slower than Pandas on purpose
questions.explain: Reading, filtering, and grouping in the example all just add steps to a plan until show() triggers execution.

questions.q: How does this differ from Pandas?
options: Pandas is eager — every line executes immediately when Python reaches it
Pandas is also lazy, identical to Spark
Pandas never executes any code until the very end of the script
There is no meaningful difference between the two
questions.explain: By the time Pandas reaches line 3, lines 1 and 2 have already fully run — unlike Spark's deferred execution.

questions.q: Why is lazy evaluation what makes Lesson 31's 'Driver builds the whole plan first' possible?
options: Because nothing has run yet, Spark can look at the whole sequence of operations at once and optimize it before executing anything
Lazy evaluation has no connection to how the Driver builds a plan
The Driver builds its plan only after every operation has already executed
Lazy evaluation prevents the Driver from ever seeing the full plan
questions.explain: This whole-plan visibility lets Spark skip unnecessary steps or combine operations — something eager execution can't do.

questions.q: In the 'common surprise' example, why does calling .filter() alone produce no visible output and no error?
options: filter() is a transformation that just builds a plan — nothing runs until an action asks for a result
filter() always throws a silent error that Spark hides
The DataFrame was empty before the filter was even called
filter() only works when combined with groupBy()
questions.explain: This is exactly why lazy evaluation surprises people coming from Pandas the first time they encounter it.

questions.q: What triggers a lazily-built plan to actually execute?
options: An action, like .show() or .count(), which explicitly requests a result
Simply writing a transformation line, with no further code needed
Restarting the Spark session
Nothing can ever trigger execution once a plan is lazy
questions.explain: This action-triggers-everything relationship is exactly what Lesson 35 names and explains in full.
